units.literal: Before long, together with Li Ye and his kind he engineered the mutiny; Yang Bin and the others—Yuming personally ran them through with his blade under the western veranda of the court hall.

units.zh: 王章女婿戶部員外郎張貽肅，血流逆註，聞者哀之。
units.en: Wang Zhang's son-in-law Zhang Yisu of the Ministry of Revenue bled so profusely that blood seemed to flow backward; all who heard of it were moved to pity.
units.literal: Wang Zhang's son-in-law Zhang Yisu, outer official of the Ministry of Revenue, had blood flowing backward—those who heard of it pitied him.

units.zh: 及北郊之敗，允明迫帝就民舍，手行弒逆，尋亦自殺。
units.en: After the defeat at the northern suburb, Yuming forced the emperor into a commoner's house and murdered him with his own hand; soon afterward he killed himself as well.
units.literal: When the northern suburb was defeated, Yuming forced the emperor into a commoner's house and personally carried out regicide; soon after he also killed himself.

units.zh: 劉銖，陜州人也。
units.en: Liu Zhu came from Shaanzhou.
units.literal: Liu Zhu was a native of Shaanzhou.

units.zh: 少事梁邵王朱友誨為牙將。
units.en: In his youth he served Prince Shao of Liang, Zhu Youhui, as a staff general.
units.literal: In youth he served Prince Shao of Liang, Zhu Youhui, as a staff general.

units.zh: 晉天福中，高祖為侍衛親軍都指揮使，與銖有舊，乃表為內職。
units.en: During the Tianfu reign of Jin, when Emperor Gaozu was commander of the palace guard, he and Zhu were old acquaintances, and Gaozu recommended him for an inner-service post.
units.literal: During Tianfu in Jin, Gaozu was commander of the palace guard personal army; he had old ties with Zhu and memorialized him for an inner-service post.

units.zh: 高祖出鎮並門，用為左都押牙。
units.en: When Gaozu was posted to govern Taiyuan, Zhu was made his left chief military adjutant.
units.literal: When Gaozu went out to govern Bing Gate, Zhu was employed as left chief military adjutant.

units.zh: 銖性慘毒好殺，高祖以為勇斷類己，深委遇之。
units.en: Zhu was cruel and bloodthirsty by nature; Gaozu thought him bold and resolute like himself and relied on him deeply.
units.literal: Zhu's nature was cruel, poisonous, and fond of killing; Gaozu thought him brave and decisive like himself and deeply entrusted and favored him.

units.zh: 國初，授永興軍節度使，從定汴、洛、移鎮青州，加同平章事。
units.en: At the dynasty's founding he was made military governor of Yongxing; he helped pacify Bian and Luoyang, was transferred to Qingzhou, and made Tongpingzhangshi.
units.literal: At the founding of the state he was appointed military governor of Yongxing Army; he followed in pacifying Bian and Luo, was transferred to govern Qingzhou, and was made Tongpingzhangshi.

units.zh: 隱帝即位，加檢校太師、兼侍中。
units.en: When Emperor Yindi came to the throne, Zhu was made honorary grand preceptor and concurrent palace secretary.
units.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded, Zhu was given the additional titles of honorary grand preceptor and concurrent palace secretary.

units.zh: 銖立法深峻，令行禁止，吏民有過，不問輕重，未嘗貸免。
units.en: Zhu's laws were harsh and strictly enforced; officials and commoners alike who offended, whether gravely or slightly, were never spared.
units.literal: Zhu made laws deep and severe; orders were enforced and prohibitions observed; if officials or commoners had offenses, without asking light or heavy, he never granted exemption.

units.zh: 每親事，小有忤旨，即令倒曳而出，至數百步外方止，膚體無完者。
units.en: Whenever he handled a case in person, the slightest offense would bring an order to drag the offender head-down for hundreds of paces; not an inch of skin was left whole.
units.literal: Whenever he personally handled affairs, if there was the slightest offense against his intent, he would order the person dragged out head downward until several hundred paces away before stopping; not a patch of skin remained whole.

units.zh: 每杖人，遣雙杖對下，謂之「合歡杖」；
units.en: When he flogged someone, he had two clubs strike together, calling it the "joyous union flogging";
units.literal: Whenever he flogged someone, he sent paired clubs down together, calling it the "joyous union club";

units.zh: 或杖人如其歲數，謂之「隨年杖」。
units.en: or he flogged a man once for each year of his age, calling it the "age-matching flogging."
units.literal: or he flogged a person according to his years of age, calling it the "age-matching club."

units.zh: 在任擅行賦斂，每秋苗一畝率錢三千，夏苗一畝錢二千，以備公用，部內畏之，脅肩重跡。
units.en: In office he levied taxes at will—three thousand cash per acre of autumn crop and two thousand per acre of summer crop for public expenses. His domain feared him; men walked with hunched shoulders and heavy tread.
units.literal: While in office he levied taxes at will; each autumn field acre averaged three thousand cash, each summer field acre two thousand, to supply public use; within his jurisdiction they feared him, shrugging shoulders and walking with heavy steps.

units.zh: 乾祐中，淄、青大蝗，銖下令捕蝗，略無遺漏，田苗無害。
units.en: During Qianyou a great locust plague struck Zi and Qing; Zhu ordered a locust hunt so thorough that scarcely one escaped, and the crops were saved.
units.literal: During Qianyou there was a great locust plague in Zi and Qing; Zhu ordered locusts captured, with hardly any missed, and the field crops were unharmed.

units.zh: 先是，濱海郡邑，皆有兩浙回易務，厚取民利，自置刑禁，追攝王民，前後長吏利其厚賂，不能禁止。
units.en: Coastal districts had long housed exchange offices of the Two Zhe, which extorted the people, enforced their own punishments, and seized imperial subjects at will; successive governors took their heavy bribes and could not stop them.
units.literal: Earlier, in coastal commanderies and districts there were exchange offices of the Two Zhe, which heavily took profit from the people, set up their own punishments and prohibitions, and pursued and seized the ruler's subjects; successive chief officials profited from their heavy bribes and could not forbid it.

units.zh: 銖即告所部，不得與吳越征負，擅行追攝，浙人惕息，莫敢幹命。
units.en: Zhu at once forbade his jurisdiction to collect debts for Wu and Yue or to pursue people on their behalf; the Zhe merchants held their breath in fear and none dared defy him.
units.literal: Zhu immediately announced to his jurisdiction that they must not collect debts for Wu and Yue or pursue and seize on their own; the people of Zhe drew in their breath in fear and none dared defy his orders.

units.zh: 朝廷懼銖之剛戾難制，因前浙州刺史郭瓊自海州用兵還，過青州，遂留之，即以府彥卿代銖，銖即時受代。
units.en: The court feared Zhu's brutal obstinacy; when former Zhe Prefect Guo Qiong returned from campaigning at Haizhou and passed through Qingzhou, he was kept there and Fu Yanqing replaced Zhu, who accepted the transfer at once.
units.literal: The court feared Zhu's stubborn violence was hard to control; because the former prefect of Zhe Guo Qiong was returning from campaigning at Haizhou and passed through Qingzhou, he was kept there and Fu Yanqing was sent to replace Zhu; Zhu immediately accepted the transfer.

units.zh: 〈（《隆平集》《郭瓊傳》云：劉銖守平盧，稱疾不朝，隱帝疑其叛，詔瓊領兵屯青州。
units.en: (The 《Longping Collection》, Biography of Guo Qiong, says: Liu Zhu held Pinglu, claimed illness, and refused to come to court; Emperor Yindi suspected rebellion and ordered Qiong to encamp at Qingzhou with troops.
units.literal: (The 《Longping Collection》, Biography of Guo Qiong, says: Liu Zhu guarded Pinglu, claimed illness and did not come to court; the Hidden Emperor suspected rebellion and ordered Qiong to lead troops and encamp at Qingzhou.

units.zh: 銖將害之，張宴伏兵幕下，瓊無懼色，銖亦不敢發。
units.en: Zhu planned to kill him and set an ambush beneath the banquet tent, but Qiong showed no fear, and Zhu did not dare strike.
units.literal: Zhu intended to harm him and spread a banquet with ambush troops beneath the tent; Qiong showed no fear, and Zhu also did not dare act.

units.zh: 瓊為言去就禍福，銖趨召。）〉
units.en: Qiong spoke to him of the consequences of staying or leaving, and Zhu hurried to obey the summons.))〉
units.literal: Qiong spoke to him of the fortune and misfortune of staying or going; Zhu hurried to answer the summons.))〉

units.zh: 離鎮之日，有私鹽數屋，雜以糞穢，填塞諸井，以土平之。
units.en: On the day he left his post he had several rooms of illicit salt mixed with filth, filled every well with it, and covered them with earth.
units.literal: On the day he left his governorship there were several rooms of private salt mixed with filth; he filled all the wells and leveled them with earth.

units.zh: 彥卿發其事以聞，銖奉朝請久之，每潛戟手於史宏肇、楊邠第。
units.en: Yanqing exposed the affair and reported it; Zhu attended court for a long time as a court gentleman and would secretly clench his fists outside the homes of Shi Hongzhao and Yang Bin.
units.literal: Yanqing exposed the matter and reported it; Zhu attended court for a long time as a court gentleman, and each time secretly clenched his fists outside the residences of Shi Hongzhao and Yang Bin.

units.zh: 會李業輩同誅宏肇等，銖喜，謂業輩曰：「君等可謂僂羅兒矣。」
units.en: When Li Ye and his allies killed Hongzhao and the others, Zhu rejoiced and told them, "You fellows have shown yourselves true hard men."
units.literal: It happened that Li Ye and his kind together executed Hongzhao and the others; Zhu was pleased and said to Ye and his kind: "You can indeed be called louluo'er."

units.zh: 尋以銖權知開封府事，周太祖親族及王峻家，並為銖所害。
units.en: Soon Zhu was made acting prefect of Kaifeng; he murdered the kin of Guo Wei and the household of Wang Jun.
units.literal: Soon Zhu was made acting administrator of Kaifeng prefecture; the Zhou ancestor's kin and Wang Jun's household were all harmed by Zhu.

units.zh: 周太祖入京城，執之下獄。
units.en: When Guo Wei entered the capital, Zhu was arrested and thrown into prison.
units.literal: When the Zhou ancestor entered the capital, Zhu was seized and imprisoned.

units.zh: 銖謂妻曰：「我則死矣，君應與人為婢耳！」
units.en: Zhu told his wife, "I am as good as dead—you will have to become someone's servant girl!"
units.literal: Zhu said to his wife: "I shall die; you will have to become someone's maidservant!"

units.zh: 妻曰：「明公所為如是，雅合為之。」
units.en: His wife replied, "Given what you have done, my lord, it is only fitting."
units.literal: His wife said: "What my lord has done is such that it is only fitting."

units.zh: 周太祖遣人讓銖曰：「昔日與公常同事漢室，寧無故人之情，家屬屠滅，公雖奉君命，加之酷毒，一何忍哉！
units.en: Guo Wei sent a man to rebuke Zhu: "We once served the Han house together—was there no bond of old friendship? You slaughtered my family; though you followed the emperor's order, to add such cruelty—how could you be so ruthless!
units.literal: The Zhou ancestor sent someone to reproach Zhu: "In former days I often served the Han house together with you—was there no feeling of old friendship? Your slaughter of my household—though you followed the ruler's command, to add such cruelty—how could you be so ruthless!

units.zh: 公家亦有妻子，還顧念否？」
units.en: You have a wife and children of your own—have you no thought for them?"
units.literal: Your household too has wife and children—do you not look back and consider?"

units.zh: 銖但稱死罪。
units.en: Zhu could only plead guilty and await death.
units.literal: Zhu could only plead guilty unto death.

units.zh: 遂啟太后，並一子誅之，而釋其妻。
units.en: He then reported to the empress dowager, executed Zhu and one son, but released his wife.
units.literal: He then reported to the empress dowager and executed Zhu together with one son, but released his wife.

units.zh: 周太祖踐阼，詔賜銖妻陜州莊宅各一區。
units.en: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou took the throne, he decreed that Zhu's wife be given an estate and a residence in Shaanzhou.
units.literal: When the Zhou ancestor took the throne, he decreed gifts to Zhu's wife of one estate and one residence each in Shaanzhou.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：漢隱帝朝，銖為開封尹，周祖自鄴起兵，銖盡誅周祖之家子孫婦女十數人，極其慘毒。
units.en: (The 《Supplementary Texts to the History of the Five Dynasties》: During Emperor Yindi's reign Zhu was prefect of Kaifeng; when the Zhou founder raised troops from Ye, Zhu slaughtered more than a dozen of Guo Wei's kin, men and women alike, with extreme cruelty.
units.literal: (The 《Supplementary Texts to the History of the Five Dynasties》: During the Hidden Emperor's Han, Zhu was prefect of Kaifeng; the Zhou ancestor raised troops from Ye; Zhu executed all of the Zhou ancestor's household—more than ten men, women, and children—with extreme cruelty.

units.zh: 及隱帝遇害，周祖以漢太后令，收銖下獄，使人責之。
units.en: After Emperor Yindi was killed, Guo Wei, by order of the Han empress dowager, arrested Zhu and sent a man to rebuke him.
units.literal: When the Hidden Emperor met with disaster, the Zhou ancestor by the Han empress dowager's order seized Zhu and imprisoned him, and sent someone to reproach him.

units.zh: 銖對曰：「某為漢家戮叛族耳，不知其他。」
units.en: Zhu replied, "I merely executed a rebel clan for the house of Han—I know nothing beyond that."
units.literal: Zhu replied: "I merely executed the rebel clan for the house of Han—I know nothing else."

units.zh: 周祖怒，遂殺之。）〉
units.en: Guo Wei in anger had him killed.))〉
units.literal: The Zhou ancestor in anger then killed him.))〉

units.zh: 史臣曰：臣觀漢之亡也，豈系於天命哉！
units.en: The historian comments: In my view, was the fall of Han really a matter of Heaven's mandate?
units.literal: The historian says: This subject observes that the fall of Han—was it bound to fate and heaven!

units.zh: 蓋委用不得其人，聽斷不符於理故也。
units.en: Rather, the wrong men were put in power, and decisions no longer accorded with reason.
units.literal: It was rather that the men entrusted and employed were not the right ones, and judgments did not accord with reason.

units.zh: 且如宏肇之淫刑，楊邠之秕政，李業、晉卿之設計，文進、允明之狂且，雖使成王為君，周公作相，亦不能保宗社之安，延歲月之命，況隱帝、逢吉之徒，其能免乎！
units.en: Consider Hongzhao's savage punishments, Yang Bin's worthless governance, the plots of Li Ye and Jinqing, the reckless arrogance of Wenjin and Yuming—even with King Cheng on the throne and the Duke of Zhou as chancellor, the dynasty could not have been saved; how then could Emperor Yindi, Fengji, and men like them have escaped ruin!
units.literal: Consider Hongzhao's excessive punishments, Yang Bin's chaff policies, Li Ye and Jinqing's plotting, Wenjin and Yuming's madness and arrogance—even if King Cheng were ruler and the Duke of Zhou chancellor, they could not preserve the security of the ancestral temple or extend the mandate of years—how much less could the Hidden Emperor, Fengji, and their kind escape!

units.zh: 《易》曰：「大君有命，開國承家，小人勿用，必亂邦也。」
units.en: The 《Book of Changes》 says: "The great ruler has a mandate to found states and establish families—petty men must not be employed, for they will surely bring the state to ruin."
units.literal: The 《Changes》 says: "The great ruler has a mandate; he founds states and inherits families—petty men must not be employed, for they will surely disorder the state."

units.zh: 當乾祐之末也，何斯言之驗歟！
units.en: At the end of Qianyou, how fully those words were fulfilled!
units.literal: At the end of Qianyou, how this saying was fulfilled!

units.zh: 惟劉銖之忍酷，又安能逭於一死乎！
units.en: As for Liu Zhu's cruelty, how could he have escaped death?
units.literal: As for Liu Zhu's cruel brutality, how could he escape a single death!
